rationaleAppend: isaiah-woh wave I-4: applied at Isa 19:1 as background in commentary. The line renders the clause conventionally, 'Behold, YHWH rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt' (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'Mounted on a swift cloud'), in lower case and without an epithet, because the verse has a predicate participle with the singular ʿāḇ and the adjective qal, not the title (overlay rokhev-al-av-qal-swift-cloud-isaiah-19). The Ugaritic attestations cited in the commentary are those printed in the project's baal-cycle-woh edition (KTU 1.2 iv 6; 1.3 ii 40; 1.3 iv 23; 1.4 vi 10). The disavowal of a vehicle reading in this entry stands. The isaiah-woh commentary reports the canon's readings of other cloud passages (TBWTT 3:107; 3:259-260) only in a final paragraph labelled speculative, and it states that the canon does not cite Isa 19.
isaiah-woh wave I-4: applied at Isa 19:1 ('the idols of Egypt shall tremble before him') and 19:3 ('they shall seek the idols'), the sites the wohChoice already names.

isaiah-woh wave I-4, chapter 19 (under wave I-4 ruling 15; the context clause itself is carried by the chapter 23 Editor's op): singular yᵉʾôr 'the Nile' at Isa 19:7 (three times) and 19:8, where ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print 'the Nile' (checked 2026-11-26), which also keeps it distinct from bare nāhār 'the river' used of the Nile at 19:5; plural yᵉʾōrê māṣôr 'the streams of Egypt' at 19:6 (ASV, JPS 1917), since 'rivers' renders nᵉhārôt in the same verse.

isaiah-woh wave I-4: 'the ground of Judah' at Isa 19:17 (ʾaḏmaṯ yᵉhûḏāh; ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS 'the land of Judah'), keeping the book's 'ground' for ʾăḏāmāh (14:1, 2; 32:13) distinct from ʾereṣ 'land' in the following verses (19:18-20).
isaiah-woh wave I-4: territorial 'the land of Egypt' at Isa 19:18, 19, 20 (ʾereṣ miṣrayim). At 19:24 bᵉqereḇ hāʾāreṣ is 'in the midst of the earth' under the overlay eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24.

isaiah-woh wave I-4: 'an altar to YHWH in the midst of the land of Egypt' (Isa 19:19); the plain noun, with the reception of the verse (the Onias temple at Leontopolis, Josephus, Antiquities 13.62-73, recalled) in commentary only.

isaiah-woh wave I-4: 'a pillar to YHWH at its border' (Isa 19:19). The prophetic text assigns a maṣṣēḇāh to YHWH in Egypt, despite the prohibition of Deut 16:22. The tension is noted in commentary, and the line keeps 'pillar' (NJPS note: 'As a symbol of the Lord's sovereignty over Egypt', checked).

isaiah-woh wave I-4: zeḇaḥ ûminḥāh 'sacrifice and meal-offering' at Isa 19:21 (ASV 'oblation'), the cultic pair; the noun tᵉnûp̄āh 'wave-offering' is not meant at Isa 19:16, where tᵉnûp̄aṯ yāḏ is the brandishing of the hand.
